title: Primary 4 Decimals
seo_title: P4 Decimals Worksheets: Free Primary 4 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Decimals up to 3 decimal places: place values, comparing and ordering, decimals as fractions, fractions as decimals (denominator a factor of 10 or 100), rounding
meta_desc: Free P4 maths practice on decimals: place value to 3 decimal places, comparing, decimals and fractions, and rounding. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Compare decimals place by place, not by how many digits they have.
body_html:
Tenths, hundredths and thousandths

Divide 1 whole into 10 equal parts: each part is 1 tenth (0.1). Divide it into 100 parts: each part is 1 hundredth (0.01). Divide it into 1000 parts: each part is 1 thousandth (0.001). Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right.

Between two hundredths there are 10 thousandths. From 0.24 to 0.25, each small space is 0.001.

Example 1

Write 3 ones, 4 tenths and 9 thousandths as a decimal.

There are 0 hundredths. Write 0 to hold the hundredths place: 3 . 4 0 9.

Answer: 3.409

Comparing and ordering

Compare the whole numbers first, then the tenths, then the hundredths, then the thousandths. It helps to give the numbers the same number of decimal places: 0.5 = 0.50 = 0.500.

Example 2

Arrange 0.5, 0.45 and 0.405 from the smallest to the greatest.

Write them with 3 decimal places: 0.500, 0.450, 0.405.

Answer: 0.405, 0.45, 0.5

Decimals and fractions

The number of decimal places tells you the denominator: 1 place is tenths, 2 places is hundredths, 3 places is thousandths. 0.3 = 310, 0.03 = 3100 and 0.003 = 31000. Then write the fraction in its simplest form.

Example 3

Express 0.25 as a fraction in its simplest form.

0.25 = 25100. Divide the numerator and denominator by 25.

Answer: 14

To change a fraction to a decimal, make an equivalent fraction with denominator 10 or 100.

Example 4

Express 320 as a decimal.

20 × 5 = 100, so 320 = 15100.

Answer: 0.15

Rounding decimals

Find the two numbers it is between. Look at the digit one place to the right of the place you are rounding to: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less rounds down. Round only once.

faq.q: What is taught in P4 decimals?
faq.a: In Primary 4, students learn place values of decimals up to 3 decimal places, compare and order decimals, change decimals to fractions and fractions to decimals, and round decimals to the nearest whole number, 1 decimal place or 2 decimal places.

faq.q: How do I explain why 0.5 is greater than 0.45?
faq.a: Write 0.5 as 0.50: it is 50 hundredths, and 0.45 is only 45 hundredths. Shading both on a hundred square shows this clearly.

faq.q: How do you round a decimal to 2 decimal places?
faq.a: Look at the 3rd digit after the decimal point: if it is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, round down. For example, 6.381 rounded to 2 decimal places is 6.38.

faq.q: Is this in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Decimals up to 3 decimal places, decimals and fractions, and rounding are part of the Primary 4 Decimals topic in the MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus. The next P4 topics add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals.

items.q: The whole square is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth. 7 full columns are shaded: 7 tenths = 710 = 0.7. 0.07 would be only 7 small squares, and 0.3 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: The whole square is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: 4 full columns (4 tenths) and 3 more small squares (3 hundredths) are shaded: 43 hundredths = 43100 = 0.43.

items.q: The whole square is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: 5 small squares are shaded and there is no full column, so there are 0 tenths. 5 hundredths = 5100 = 0.05. Write 0 in the tenths place.

items.q: 1 whole is divided into 1000 equal parts. What decimal is 1 part?
items.e: Each part is 11000 of the whole, 1 thousandth: 0.001. 0.01 is 1 hundredth (100 parts) and 0.1 is 1 tenth (10 parts).

items.q: What decimal is shown in the place value chart?
items.e: 7 ones, 0 tenths and 6 hundredths: 7.06. The 0 holds the tenths place. 7.6 drops the 0, so the 6 moves to the tenths place.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 2.635?
items.e: The red 5 is in the 3rd place after the decimal point, the thousandths place. Its value is 5 thousandths = 0.005.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 0.482?
items.e: The red 8 is in the 2nd place after the decimal point, the hundredths place. Its value is 8 hundredths = 0.08.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 14.307?
items.e: The red 3 is in the 1st place after the decimal point, the tenths place. Its value is 3 tenths = 0.3.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in 3.024?
items.e: In 3.024 the 4 is in the thousandths place, the 3rd place after the point. It stands for 0.004.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in 0.951?
items.e: In 0.951 the 9 is in the tenths place, the 1st place after the point. It stands for 0.9.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 2 in 25.168?
items.e: In 25.168 the 2 is in the tens place (2 places to the left of the point). It stands for 20.

items.q: In 6.583, which digit is in the thousandths place?
items.e: Count the places after the decimal point: tenths (5), hundredths (8), thousandths (3). The answer is 3.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: From 0.24 to 0.25 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 thousandth (0.001). The dot is 7 spaces after 0.24: 0.247. 0.253 counts back from the wrong end.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: From 1.3 to 1.4 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth (0.01). The dot is 8 spaces after 1.30: 1.38. 1.308 would be very close to 1.3.

items.q: How many thousandths are there in 0.4?
items.e: 1 tenth = 100 thousandths, so 4 tenths = 400 thousandths. 0.4 = 0.400.
4 ones, 3 tenths, 0 hundredths and 8 thousandths: 4 . 3 0 8 = 4.308. 4.38 drops the 0 that holds the hundredths place.

items.q: Write 3 ones, 4 tenths and 9 thousandths as a decimal.
items.e: There are 0 hundredths, so write one digit in each place: 3 . 4 0 9 = 3.409. The 0 holds the hundredths place.

items.q: Write 2 tens, 6 hundredths and 5 thousandths as a decimal.
items.e: 2 tens = 20. There are 0 ones and 0 tenths. Then 6 hundredths and 5 thousandths: 20.065.

items.q: Which is equal to 5.274?
items.e: 5 ones, 2 tenths, 7 hundredths and 4 thousandths: 5 + 0.2 + 0.07 + 0.004.

items.q: What is 0.01 more than 4.293?
items.e: 0.01 is 1 hundredth. The hundredths digit is 9, and 9 + 1 = 10 hundredths = 1 more tenth. So 4.293 + 0.01 = 4.303. 4.294 adds 0.001 and 4.393 adds 0.1.

items.q: Compare 0.45 and 0.5. Which is correct?
items.e: 0.5 = 0.50, so the second square has 50 hundredths shaded. 45 hundredths < 50 hundredths, so 0.45 < 0.5. Do not compare 45 with 5: the 5 in 0.5 is 5 tenths.

items.q: Compare 0.7 and 0.70. Which is correct?
items.e: A zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 7 tenths = 70 hundredths. So 0.7 = 0.70.

items.q: Compare 2.305 and 2.35. Which is correct?
items.e: Both have 2 ones and 3 tenths. Compare the hundredths: 0 < 5. So 2.305 < 2.35, even though 2.305 has more digits.

items.q: Compare 0.089 and 0.1. Which is correct?
items.e: Compare the tenths: 0.089 has 0 tenths and 0.1 has 1 tenth. So 0.089 < 0.1, even though 89 > 1.

items.q: Compare 6.42 and 6.402. Which is correct?
items.e: Write 6.42 as 6.420. Both have 6 ones and 4 tenths. Compare the hundredths: 2 > 0. So 6.42 > 6.402.

items.q: Compare 13.1 and 9.999. Which is correct?
items.e: Compare the whole numbers first: 13 > 9. So 13.1 > 9.999, even though 9.999 has more digits.

items.q: Which decimal is the greatest?
items.e: Compare the tenths: 6, 5, 5 and 0. 0.6 has the most tenths, so it is the greatest, even though 0.594 and 0.599 have more digits.

items.q: Which decimal is the smallest?
items.e: 0.53 has 5 tenths, so it is the greatest. The others have 3 tenths: compare the hundredths 0, 5 and 5. 0.305 has 0 hundredths, so it is the smallest.

items.q: Which number is greater than 0.25?
items.e: 0.25 = 0.250 and 0.3 = 0.300. 300 thousandths > 250 thousandths, so 0.3 > 0.25. 0.249 is 1 thousandth less than 0.25.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 0.4?
items.e: 0.4 = 4 tenths = 400 thousandths = 0.400. Zeros at the end do not change the value. 0.04 and 0.004 move the 4 to a smaller place.

items.q: Which number is between 1.25 and 1.26?
Which letter shows 0.355?
items.e: Each space is 0.01. 0.355 is halfway between 0.35 and 0.36. That is point B. A is 0.32, C is 0.37 and D is 0.395.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: 0.8 = 0.80, and 80 hundredths > 79 hundredths. So 0.8 > 0.79 is true.

items.q: Hui Min says 0.125 > 0.2 because 125 > 2. Which is correct?
items.e: Compare the tenths first: 0.125 has 1 tenth and 0.2 has 2 tenths. So 0.125 < 0.2. Or write 0.2 as 0.200: 125 thousandths < 200 thousandths.

items.q: Arrange from the smallest to the greatest: 0.5, 0.45, 0.405
items.e: Write them with 3 decimal places: 0.500, 0.450, 0.405. 405 < 450 < 500, so the order is 0.405, 0.45, 0.5. The longest number is not the greatest.

items.q: Arrange from the smallest to the greatest: 3.2, 3.02, 3.202, 3.022
items.e: All have 3 ones. Write them with 3 decimal places: 3.200, 3.020, 3.202, 3.022. 20 < 22 < 200 < 202 thousandths, so 3.02, 3.022, 3.2, 3.202.

items.q: Arrange from the greatest to the smallest: 0.9, 0.09, 0.909, 0.099

Which digit can go in the box to make this true?
0.6□4 > 0.67
items.e: Write 0.67 as 0.670. Both numbers have 6 tenths, so compare the hundredths. The box must be 7 or more: 0.684 > 0.670. So 8 works. With 6, 0.664 < 0.670.

items.q: Use the digits 4, 0 and 7 once each to fill 0.□□□. What is the greatest decimal you can make?
items.e: Put the greatest digit in the greatest place: 7 tenths, then 4 hundredths, then 0 thousandths. The greatest decimal is 0.740.

items.q: What is the smallest number with 3 decimal places that is greater than 2.39?
items.e: 2.39 = 2.390. The next thousandth after 2.390 is 2.391. 2.390 is equal to 2.39, not greater, and 2.389 is smaller.

items.q: Write 310 as a decimal.
items.e: 310 is 3 tenths. Tenths are the 1st place after the point: 0.3. 0.03 is 3 hundredths.

items.q: Write 7100 as a decimal.
items.e: 7100 is 7 hundredths. Hundredths need 2 places, so write 0 in the tenths place: 0.07.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.3?
items.e: 0.3 has 1 digit after the point, so it means tenths: 0.3 = 310. 3100 is 0.03, not 0.3.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.09?
items.e: 0.09 has 2 digits after the point, so it means hundredths: 9 hundredths = 9100.

items.q: Write 0.047 as a fraction.
items.e: 0.047 has 3 digits after the point, so it means thousandths: 471000. 47100 would be 0.47.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 12?
items.e: Make tenths: 12 = 510 (multiply the numerator and denominator by 5). 5 tenths = 0.5. 1.2 just writes the digits 1 and 2.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 15?
items.e: Make tenths: 15 = 210 (multiply the numerator and denominator by 2). 2 tenths = 0.2. 0.15 just writes the 1 and the 5 after the point.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 34?
items.e: Make hundredths: 34 = 75100 (multiply the numerator and denominator by 25). 75 hundredths = 0.75. 0.25 is 14, the part that is left.

items.q: Express 0.5 as a fraction in its simplest form.
items.e: 0.5 = 510. Divide the numerator and denominator by 5: 510 = 12. 15 is 0.2, not 0.5.

items.q: Express 0.6 as a fraction in its simplest form.
items.e: 0.6 = 610. Divide the numerator and denominator by 2: 35. 6100 is 0.06, and 25 is 0.4.

items.q: Express 0.25 as a fraction in its simplest form.
items.e: 0.25 = 25100. Divide the numerator and denominator by 25: 14. 25 just uses the digits 2 and 5.

items.q: Express 0.04 as a fraction in its simplest form.
items.e: 0.04 = 4100. Divide the numerator and denominator by 4: 125. 14 is 0.25 and 25 is 0.4.

items.q: The whole square is 1. Which is not equal to the shaded part?
items.e: 4 full columns are shaded: 4 tenths. 0.4 = 410 = 25, so they all match. 0.04 is only 4 small squares.

items.q: Express 320 as a decimal.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so make hundredths: 320 = 15100 = 0.15. 0.32 and 3.2 just write the digits 3 and 2.

items.q: Express 925 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so make hundredths: 925 = 36100 = 0.36. 0.18 multiplies the numerator by 2 instead of 4.

items.q: Express 750 as a decimal.
items.e: 50 × 2 = 100, so make hundredths: 750 = 14100 = 0.14. 0.07 forgets to multiply the numerator by 2.

items.q: Express 2 35 as a decimal.
items.e: 35 = 610, so 2 35 = 2 + 0.6 = 2.6. 2.35 just writes the digits 3 and 5.

items.q: Ryan says 0.3 = 3100. Which is correct?
c: 0.3 is 3 tenths, so 0.3 = 310
Ryan is right: 0.3 = 3100
items.e: The 3 is in the 1st place after the point, the tenths place. So 0.3 = 310. 3100 is 0.03 (2 places).

items.q: Express 4.08 as a mixed number in its simplest form.
items.e: 4.08 = 4 + 8100. Divide the numerator and denominator by 4: 8100 = 225. So 4.08 = 4 225. 4 45 is 4.8 (it drops the 0 in the tenths place).

items.q: Arrange from the smallest to the greatest: 0.6, 12, 0.45
items.e: Change 12 to a decimal: 0.5. Now compare 0.60, 0.50 and 0.45: 0.45, 12, 0.6. 12 is not the smallest just because 1 and 2 are small digits.

items.q: Round 4.65 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 4.65 is between 4 and 5. Look at the tenths digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up to 5. The nearest whole number has no decimal places, so 4.7 is not the answer.

items.q: Round 7.38 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 7.38 is between 7 and 8. Look at the tenths digit: 3. It is 4 or less, so round down to 7. 7.38 is closer to 7 than to 8.

items.q: Round the number at the red dot (12.6) to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 12.6 is between 12 and 13. Look at the tenths digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up to 13. The dot is closer to 13 than to 12.

items.q: Round the number at the red dot (2.47) to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 2.47 is between 2.4 and 2.5. Look at the hundredths digit: 7. It is 5 or more, so round up to 2.5. The dot is closer to 2.5 than to 2.4.

items.q: Round 15.55 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 15.55 is between 15 and 16. Look at the tenths digit: 5. It is 5 or more, so round up to 16. Rounding to the nearest whole number gives an answer with no decimal places.

items.q: Round 6.32 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 6.32 is between 6.3 and 6.4. Look at the hundredths digit: 2. It is 4 or less, so round down to 6.3. 6.4 rounds up when the digit is only 2.

items.q: Round 8.47 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: 8.47 is between 8 and 9. Look at the tenths digit: 4. It is 4 or less, so round down to 8. 9 comes from rounding twice (8.47 → 8.5 → 9). Round only once, using the tenths digit.

items.q: Round 0.746 to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 0.746 is between 0.74 and 0.75. Look at the thousandths digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up to 0.75. 0.7 rounds to 1 decimal place instead of 2.

items.q: Round 6.381 to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 6.381 is between 6.38 and 6.39. Look at the thousandths digit: 1. It is 4 or less, so round down to 6.38. 6.4 rounds to 1 decimal place instead of 2.

items.q: To round 8.274 to 2 decimal places, which digit do you look at?
items.e: To round to 2 decimal places, look one place to the right of the hundredths: the thousandths digit. It is 4, so 8.274 rounds down to 8.27.

items.q: Round 7.049 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 7.049 is between 7.0 and 7.1. Look at the hundredths digit: 4. It is 4 or less, so round down to 7.0. The answer is written 7.0 to show 1 decimal place. Do not round the 9 first: 7.049 is closer to 7.0 than to 7.1.

items.q: Round 3.952 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 3.952 is between 3.9 and 4.0. Look at the hundredths digit: 5. It is 5 or more, so round up to 4.0. The answer is written 4.0 to show 1 decimal place. 3.10 is wrong: 10 tenths make 1 whole.

items.q: Round 12.045 to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 12.045 is between 12.04 and 12.05. Look at the thousandths digit: 5. It is 5 or more, so round up to 12.05. 12.45 drops the 0 in the tenths place.

items.q: Which number rounds to 5.3 when it is rounded to 1 decimal place?
items.e: Look at the hundredths digit. 5.348 has 4 hundredths, so it rounds down to 5.3 (do not round the 8 first). 5.351 and 5.36 round up to 5.4, and 5.249 rounds to 5.2.

items.q: Which number becomes 6 when it is rounded to the nearest whole number?
items.e: 5.5 is between 5 and 6. The tenths digit is 5, so it rounds up to 6. 6.5 and 6.51 round to 7, and 5.49 rounds to 5.

items.q: A number was rounded to 1 decimal place. The answer is 3.6. Which could be the number?
items.e: 3.58 is between 3.5 and 3.6. The hundredths digit is 8, so it rounds up to 3.6. 3.65 and 3.67 round to 3.7, and 3.54 rounds to 3.5.

items.q: Round 9.96 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 9.96 is between 9.9 and 10.0. Look at the hundredths digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up to 10.0. The answer is written 10.0 to show 1 decimal place. 9 tenths and 1 more make 10 tenths, which is 1 whole.

items.q: Round 2.396 to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 2.396 is between 2.39 and 2.40. Look at the thousandths digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up to 2.40. The answer is written 2.40 to show 2 decimal places. 9 hundredths and 1 more make 10 hundredths, which is 1 more tenth.

items.q: A number with 1 decimal place is rounded to the nearest whole number. The answer is 8. What is the smallest the number can be?
items.e: 7.5 is the smallest number with 1 decimal place that rounds up to 8 (the tenths digit is 5). 7.4 rounds down to 7. 8.4 is the greatest it can be, and 8.5 rounds to 9.

items.q: Round 0.999 to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 0.999 is between 0.99 and 1.00. Look at the thousandths digit: 9. It is 5 or more, so round up to 1.00. The answer is written 1.00 to show 2 decimal places.

items.q: How long is the pencil?
items.e: The pencil ends 4 small marks after 7 cm. Each small mark is 1 mm = 0.1 cm, so the length is 7.4 cm. 7.04 cm would be only a tiny bit more than 7 cm. 7.3 cm counts the 7 cm line as the first small mark.
There are 10 small marks between 2 kg and 3 kg, so each small mark is 0.1 kg. The needle is 7 small marks after 2 kg: 2.7 kg. 2.3 kg counts back from 3 kg.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each small mark is 0.1 ℓ. The water level is at the line labelled 0.6: 0.6 ℓ. 0.4 ℓ is the empty part of the jug.

items.q: Write 5 dollars 40 cents in dollars.
items.e: 40 cents = 40 hundredths of a dollar = $0.40. So 5 dollars 40 cents = $5.40. $5.04 is 5 dollars 4 cents.

items.q: Write 85¢ in dollars.
items.e: 100¢ = $1, so 85¢ = 85 hundredths of a dollar = $0.85. $8.50 is 850¢ and $0.08 is only 8¢.

items.q: A packet of chicken rice costs $3.05. Which is the same amount?
items.e: In $3.05 the 0 is in the tenths place and the 5 is in the hundredths place. So $3.05 is 3 dollars 5 cents. 3 dollars 50 cents is $3.50.

items.q: Ali has these coins in his pocket. How much money does he have?
A bowl of laksa at a hawker centre costs $4.85. What is the price to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $4.85 is between $4 and $5. Look at the tenths digit: 8. It is 5 or more, so round up to $5. $4.90 rounds to the nearest 10¢, not the nearest dollar.

items.q: Wei Ming’s EZ-Link card has $12.45 left on it. What is this amount to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $12.45 is between $12 and $13. The tenths digit is 4, so round down to $12. $13 comes from rounding twice ($12.45 → $12.50 → $13).

items.q: Siti’s ribbon is 1.25 m long. Farah’s ribbon is 1.3 m long. Whose ribbon is longer?
items.e: 1.3 m = 1.30 m. 30 hundredths > 25 hundredths, so Farah’s ribbon is longer. The bar model shows Farah’s bar is longer. 1.25 has more digits, but that does not make it greater.

items.q: On Sports Day, Ahmad jumps 2.45 m and Ryan jumps 2.405 m in the long jump. Who jumps farther?
items.e: Write both with 3 decimal places: 2.450 m and 2.405 m. 450 > 405 thousandths, so Ahmad jumps farther. 2.405 has more digits, but that does not make it greater.

items.q: Mr Tan cuts a 1 m ribbon into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 4 units = 1 m, so 1 unit = 14 m. 14 = 25100 = 0.25 m. 0.4 m is a common mistake: 14 is not 0.4.

items.q: Chloe pours 1 ℓ of orange juice equally into 5 cups. How much juice is in each cup? Give your answer as a decimal.
items.e: 5 units = 1 ℓ, so 1 unit = 15 ℓ. 15 = 210 = 0.2 ℓ. 0.5 ℓ would fill only 2 cups.

items.q: Mdm Wong uses 34 kg of flour to bake kueh for Hari Raya Puasa. Write this mass as a decimal.
items.e: 34 = 75100 = 0.75 kg. 0.34 kg just writes the digits 3 and 4.

items.q: Kavya’s water bottle holds 0.6 ℓ. What fraction of a litre is that? Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: 0.6 = 610 = 35. 6100 ℓ is only 0.06 ℓ.

items.q: In a 100 m race, Wei Ming takes 15.36 s, Jun Jie takes 15.4 s, Hafiz takes 15.29 s and Ethan takes 15.3 s. Who is the fastest?
items.e: The fastest runner takes the least time. Write the times with 2 decimal places: 15.36, 15.40, 15.29 and 15.30. 15.29 is the smallest, so Hafiz is the fastest. Jun Jie’s 15.4 s is the slowest, not the fastest.

items.q: Mrs Ng buys three durians with masses of 2.5 kg, 2.35 kg and 2.475 kg. Arrange the masses from the lightest to the heaviest.
items.e: Write them with 3 decimal places: 2.500, 2.350 and 2.475. 350 < 475 < 500, so the order is 2.35 kg, 2.475 kg, 2.5 kg.

items.q: A durian has a mass of 1.846 kg. What is its mass, rounded to 1 decimal place?
items.e: 1.846 is between 1.8 and 1.9. Look at the hundredths digit: 4. It is 4 or less, so round down to 1.8. So the durian is about 1.8 kg. 1.9 kg comes from rounding twice (1.846 → 1.85 → 1.9).

items.q: Kumar is 1.376 m tall. What is his height, rounded to 2 decimal places?
items.e: 1.376 is between 1.37 and 1.38. Look at the thousandths digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up to 1.38. So Kumar is about 1.38 m tall.

items.q: At recess, Devi drinks 0.6 ℓ of water and Raju drinks 0.58 ℓ. Raju says he drank more because 58 > 6. Who drank more?
items.e: 0.6 ℓ = 0.60 ℓ. 60 hundredths > 58 hundredths, so Devi drank more. Compare place by place: 6 tenths > 5 tenths.
